## The hotspot picture

Pulling the three finding types together, ranked by how much of the repo each file touches:

| File | fan-in | fan-out | size | biggest function | transitive importers |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `src/utils.ts` | **18** | 1 | 425 L | — | 29 |
| `src/plugin.ts` | **10** | 3 | — | `buildFinished` 103 L | 29 |
| `src/log.ts` | 9 | 0 | — | — | **30** |
| `src/index.ts` | 4 | **17** | 460 L | `build` 293 L | 7 |
| `src/esbuild/index.ts` | 1 | **11** | — | `runEsbuild` 237 L | 7 |
| `src/rollup.ts` | 0 | 7 | — | `getRollupConfig` 122 L | 0 |
| `src/api-extractor.ts` | 1 | 6 | — | `rollupDtsFiles` 85 L | 7 |
| `test/utils.ts` | 9 | 0 | — | — | 9 (tests) |
| `docs/README.md` | — | — | 679 L | — | 0 |

The p95 cutoffs (fan-in 9, fan-out 6) put eight files in the top connectivity tier, but they split cleanly into two very different kinds of risk: **high fan-in = expensive to change, cheap to leave alone**; **high fan-out = big and messy, but almost nobody depends on its internals**.

## Triage order

**1. `src/index.ts` — refactor first.** It is the single largest concentration of mess in the repo: 460 lines, and seven `large_function` findings stacked inside it — `build` at 293 L (4.9× threshold, the worst multiplier anywhere), a 274 L anonymous body nested inside it, `mainTasks` at 194 L, `normalizeOptions` 96 L, `startWatcher` 79 L, `buildAll` 75 L. Crucially its **fan-in is only 4** — it imports 17 things but almost nothing imports it. Extracting helpers here is nearly ripple-free: you're restructuring a leaf-of-the-graph orchestrator. Highest mess-to-exposure ratio in the codebase, so it's the cheapest big win.

**2. `src/esbuild/index.ts` — refactor second.** Fan-out 11 sits exactly at the p99 cutoff, but **fan-in is 1**. `runEsbuild` is 237 lines with a 38-property options bag (`crime_00054`) and two `Date.now()` calls buried at L98 and L278. One importer means you can split this aggressively with essentially no coordination cost. Same logic as #1, one tier down in size.

**3. `src/utils.ts` — the actual blast-radius reduction, but do it carefully.** Fan-in **18** is the highest in the repo and it fans out to **29 transitive importers**; it's also 425 lines with 7 sync I/O calls across `removeFiles`/`ensureTempDeclarationDir`. This is the file where splitting genuinely shrinks future blast radius — every one of those 18 importers currently pulls in a 425-line kitchen sink to get one helper. But it's third, not first, because the same 18 importers make it the most expensive mistake. Do it as a **mechanical move behind a re-export barrel**: split by responsibility (fs helpers, path helpers, format helpers), keep `src/utils.ts` re-exporting everything, migrate importers later. Zero call-site churn on day one.

**4. `src/plugin.ts` — internals only, do not restructure the interface.** Fan-in 10 puts it at the p99 cutoff with 29 transitive importers, and `buildFinished` is 103 lines. Extract helpers *inside* `buildFinished`; leave the exported surface untouched. The finding's own `treat_as_load_bearing` action is right here — the fan-in number says the cost of a signature change is 10 direct edits and a 29-file ripple, which no amount of tidiness justifies.

## Leave alone

- **`src/log.ts`** — fan-in 9, **fan-out 0**, and the highest transitive reach in the whole repo (30 importers). But it has *no* structural finding: the only crime is two unprefixed booleans (`onlyImportant`, `silent`). This is what a healthy leaf module looks like — maximum reach, minimum internal complexity. Touching it buys nothing and risks 30 files. Rename the booleans if you're already in there; otherwise don't open it.
- **`docs/README.md`** — the highest-severity `large_file` (679 lines, 2.3× threshold) and completely irrelevant to blast radius: **0 importers**, it's documentation. This is the clearest case in the report of severity ≠ priority. Suppress it or ignore it.
- **`src/rollup.ts`** — `getRollupConfig` is 122 lines and misleadingly named (it calls `setSilent` and `removeFiles` despite the `get` prefix, `crime_00053`). But **fan-in 0** — nothing imports this file, so refactoring it reduces blast radius by exactly zero. Fix it when you're next editing it for a real reason.
- **`src/cli-main.ts`** — `main` is 153 lines, but fan-in 2 and blast radius 0.04. Local mess, not systemic.
- **`test/utils.ts`** — fan-in 9 looks alarming until you notice the 9 importers are all tests. Contained.
- **`src/api-extractor.ts`** — fan-out 6 is exactly at the p95 line, i.e. the weakest possible qualifier. Defer.

## One caveat that should gate all of this

Every finding in this report has `churn: 0` — there's no git history signal, so this ranking is purely structural. If the fixture had real history, churn would likely reorder the middle of the list.

More seriously: the report contains **16 `weak_test_signal` findings**, including 11 tests with literally zero `expect` calls across `test/index.test.ts`, `test/dts.test.ts`, `test/tsconfig.test.ts`, and `test/shims.test.ts`. Refactoring `src/utils.ts` — 29 transitive importers — against a suite where a meaningful fraction of tests only prove the code ran is doing it without a net. I'd put assertions on the `dts` and `tsconfig` tests *before* step 3, not after.
